method: I read the six reports, then re-opened evidence/ myself and re-measured every load-bearing number with python3 (PIL 12.3.0, numpy 2.4.6, cv2 5.0.0) and toolchain/ffmpeg/ffprobe. Clips were decoded to PNG with ffmpeg -vsync 0 and read on the app's timebase declared in frames.json (step_ms 16 for every run of every clip, playback_over_app_time 1.0; ffprobe confirms r_frame_rate 125/2 = 62.5 fps and nb_frames matching MANIFEST for all five clips, so frame index = app step). Specific re-measurements: (a) the anti-goal 'simulated paper' detector re-implemented at its own stated thresholds and at looser ones, on all ten stills plus crops/dusk_pulse.png; (b) edge straightness as the standard deviation of the first bright row per column / first bright column per row over a component's full extent; (c) interior texture as the standard deviation of the image minus a sigma-4 Gaussian blur; (d) contact shadow by the same recipe material_truth used - paper mask at luminance>170, morphological close 9x9, hole-fill, near-black tear ink at luminance<65 excluded, cv2.distanceTransform bands at 2-5 / 5-10 / 10-20 / 60-120 px - run on all ten stills plus dusk_pulse rather than two; (e) tear-mask repetition by detrending each paper element's top-edge profile and cross-correlating every pair within a screen, with two real notes in 02_chat.png as the control; (f) day-versus-dusk lighting response by applying a fixed day-derived mask to both 01_pulse.png and crops/dusk_pulse.png and comparing mean RGB and R/B ratio per object; (g) page motion by cv2.phaseCorrelate on the bottom nav band (rows 2180-2340) of consecutive frames of 08_state_propagating.mp4; (h) repeated frames by adjacent mean-absolute-difference over all 502 frames of 08 and all 256 of 06; (i) contrast as WCAG sRGB relative luminance with the percentile pairs the report named; (j) scroll_webkit.json recomputed from per_frame; (k) hand.json's method re-implemented from scratch (connected components of ink, each normalised to 32x32, pairwise IoU); (l) haptics.json's 36 waveforms re-tested for collision at 1/20/40/60/80 ms grids and under a harder same-pulse-count/same-duration test; (m) audio streams of 07 and 15 demuxed to 8 kHz mono and RMS-enveloped against their sound.json placements. Every number below is reproducible from evidence/ alone. I did not open evidence/SCORE.json, any other evidence/critics/ directory, docs/, source, or git.

gaps.kind: affirmative claim the evidence contradicts
gaps.what: One torn-edge mask is repeated twelve times down 12_search.png, which is the 'tiled repeating texture' clause of the no-simulated-paper anti-goal, and it stands directly against material_truth's what_is_working #1 ('Tear masks do not repeat on a single screen ... the largest normalised match is 0.305; no pair exceeds 0.31') and anti_goal's 'Real notes carry irregular torn contours (evidence/logs/tears.json: 8 visible, 8 distinct, no repeats)'. Both statements were measured only on 02_chat.png's event notes; neither critic looked at chrome paper or at any other screen. 03_us.png carries the same defect once.
gaps.measurement: 12_search.png: twelve full-width filter strips at y 680-774, 838-937, 997-1094, 1156-1254, 1314-1414, 1473-1573, 1633-1729, 1792-1888, 1951-2048, 2110-2206, 2267-2368, 2428-2524. Detrending each strip's top-edge profile over columns x=100-1349 gives per-strip standard deviations of 10.2-12.8 px and ranges of 30-38 px, so these are genuinely ragged edges, not flat ones. Pairwise Pearson correlation of the detrended profiles: median 0.994 over 66 pairs, 102 of the 105 pairs formed among all 15 ragged bands exceed r=0.80, the pair (2110-2206, 2428-2524) reaches r=1.000, and strip 0 against strip 6 gives r=0.9944 with a mean absolute difference of 1.117 px and a maximum of 2.7 px. Control: the two real notes in 02_chat.png at y 541-991 and y 1780-2274 give r=0.208 with a mean absolute difference of 13.13 px. 03_us.png: the date card at y 689-1248 and the todo card at y 2420-2722 correlate at r=0.998. Same detector on 02_chat, 13_messenger_states, 04_moments, 01_pulse, 17_setup_pwa and dusk_pulse: zero pairs above r=0.74.
gaps.where: evidence/12_search.png y 680-2524 full width; evidence/03_us.png y 689-1248 against y 2420-2722; control evidence/02_chat.png

gaps.kind: detector that cannot see what it was pointed at

The forbidden shape is not a transient composing placeholder in one clip; it is the five-tab bar at the foot of ten of the eleven stills, the search chip, and the Us glance cards.

The same five slabs, 266-267 px wide with a top-edge standard deviation of 0.00 over 266 columns, are present in 01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings, 10_first_run, 12_search, 13_messenger_states, 17_setup_pwa and crops/dusk_pulse (absent only from 14_media_viewer). 03_us.png TO DO glance card, 708x163 px: top edge standard deviation 0.00 over 708 columns, left edge 0.00 over 163 rows, shadow below running 74.4 -> 83.1 against a desk at 94.0. 04_moments.png 'noor' filter chip: top and left edge standard deviation 0.00, shadow 72.3 -> 85.1. Running anti_goal's own thresholds (fill>=0.985, w>300, h>80) over all eleven stills reproduces its null result exactly - 0 hits everywhere - confirming the null is a threshold artefact, since the same detector finds the composing card in 207 of 256 frames of 06_unfolding.mp4.

gaps.kind: artifact nobody opened, carrying a defect
gaps.what: The modelled feeling objects do not take the scene's light. evidence/crops/dusk_pulse.png is a second, genuinely different render of the Pulse desk under dusk (it is not a colour grade of the day frame: binning day values in 32-level buckets, the dusk value within a bucket still varies by 21-62 levels per channel, so the mapping is spatially varying). Under that light every paper surface shifts and warms, but the two fully modelled objects barely move and take no warm cast at all - they are pre-lit sprites composited into both lightings. This contradicts material_truth's what_is_working #4 ('the landing object is real geometry ... one light from upper-left').

gaps.kind: the same thing is not the same thing everywhere

Three events appear in both 12_search and 13_messenger_states, and all three are given a different tear mask in the two artifacts while their paper stock stays identical. gaps.kind: blocking verdict resting on an inference the log warns against
gaps.what: Every number in the scroll-jank blocking finding reproduces exactly, but the log cannot carry the conclusion. logs/scroll_webkit.json's own note reads 'one frame per harness step, so these are the cost of drawing a frame, not a measured refresh rate', and its over_16ms field is 809 of 809 - every frame, including the 14 ms ones, because raster alone is 164 ms with no GPU. Nothing in evidence/ separates an app-side rebuild on every third frame from a harness that forces a relayout on every third driven step, and the critic itself says 11_chat_scroll.mp4 cannot corroborate it. A blocking severity is more than this single log can support; serious is what it can.
gaps.measurement: Recomputed from per_frame (809 entries): 243 frames at build_ms >= 900 (30.0%), range 938-1651, median 1134; the other 566 have a median of 14; inter-heavy gaps are 3 in 173 of 242 cases, 4 in 36, 5 in 24; heavy frames account for 283,567 of 293,356 total build ms (96.67%); raster p50 164, p95 188, max 226. gaps.kind: claim contradicted by the report's own measurement
gaps.what: 'The hand is monoline with no pressure signature' is stated over numbers that show a two-fold spread inside a single line, and the sharper reading of the same evidence is available in a log no critic set beside hand.json. The repeat half of the finding is sound and I confirm it independently; the pressure half is not carried by what is printed.
gaps.measurement: The report's own figures are p10 4.0, p50 6.0, p90 8.0 device px on each of two lines - p90 is twice p10, which is variation, not a constant weight. My independent re-implementation of hand.json's method on 02_chat.png (ink < 120, connected components, each normalised to 32x32, pairwise IoU) gives 388 marks, median best-fit IoU 0.653, p90 0.867, max 1.000, and 45 marks with a twin at IoU >= 0.85 - against hand.json's 491 marks, 0.628, 0.843, 1.0 and 45 twins, so the log reproduces. The identical pair is a 13 x 23 px glyph of 91 ink pixels, not a dot, so 'at least one pair of marks is identical once normalised' stands. logs/fonts.json, opened only by the code critic and only for the DeskStamp issue, gives the diagnosis: both faces carry 775 glyphs with 5 variants, and over 4,000 texts the share of glyphs drawing a repeated variant is 0.3006 against a floor of 0.2 (0.4039 if the step were fixed). The finding is 'five variants per glyph is too few', not 'this is a font'.

anti_goal.why: The fourth anti-goal does not fail only in a transient composing placeholder; it fails in the app's permanent chrome on every screen, and the report cleared the stills using a detector that structurally cannot see it. Five tab slabs sit at the foot of ten of eleven stills with a top-edge standard deviation of 0.00 px over 266 columns, a left edge of 0.00 over 124 rows, an interior high-pass standard deviation of 1.20 grey levels against 19.3-27.3 for the note paper in the same frame, and a drop shadow running 78.4 -> 91.1 over 11 px; the Us glance card is 708x163 with a 0.00 top edge and its own shadow; the Moments chips and the search chip are the same shape. Separately, the 'tiled repeating texture' clause fails outright: twelve filter strips on 12_search.png share one torn-edge mask at a median pairwise correlation of 0.994 with one pair at 1.000, against a control of 0.21 between two real notes. The report's placeholder finding is correct and reproduces to the frame (207 of 256), and its emoji, voice and self-naming work is sound and I confirm it, but the paper anti-goal is failed by the permanent furniture of the app rather than by one card in one clip.

material_truth.why: Its blocking findings hold and I confirm and extend them - no contact shadow on any of eleven stills, and the 'goodnight' black plane is present in a second lighting too - but one of its what_is_working items is false and a second is unsupported. Tear masks do repeat on a single screen: twelve on 12_search.png at a median r of 0.994 and one pair on 03_us.png at 0.998; the report's 'no pair exceeds 0.31' was measured on 02_chat.png alone. And the feeling objects are not lit by the scene: under dusk, paper shifts 30-43 mean RGB levels and warms (status note R/B 1.077 -> 1.270) while the 'goodnight' card shifts 7.8 and does not warm at all (1.051 -> 1.064), so 'real geometry ... one light from upper-left' describes a pre-lit sprite. Two of its own numbers also do not survive - the 712 px constant width (711 in 193 of 207 frames, six distinct widths overall) and 'monoline with no pressure signature' over a p10-to-p90 spread of 2x.

messenger_reliability.why: Everything it measured reproduces - the reply chip at 1.35:1 and the attach sheet at 2.05:1 to two decimals, the empty video sliver, the twelve filter strips over one hit, the 12,289 / 12,363 / 12,577 ms fresh loads against 2,487-2,739 kept, and every scroll_webkit figure exactly. Two adjustments pull in opposite directions and net upward by a point. Down: the scroll-jank finding is scored blocking on a log whose own note says these are the cost of drawing a frame and not a refresh rate, whose over_16ms is 809 of 809 because raster alone is 164 ms with no GPU, and which cannot distinguish an app rebuild from a harness relayout on every third driven step - serious, not blocking. Up: it marked the messenger down partly for un-evidenced setup and pairing while 17_setup_pwa.png sat unopened, and that artifact shows the iPhone home-screen install, the tailnet step, the certificate-trust step and the six-word pairing on paper in the app's own voice, which is real evidence for a named mission requirement.

coherence.why: Its strongest claim reproduces exactly - the top 230 rows of the seven region artifacts differ pairwise by a mean of at most 0.0009 of 255 - and its video-row and missing-Android findings are right. But two coherence questions went unasked and both fail. The same note carries a different torn edge in two artifacts while its paper stock stays the same, and the tear list is identical in positional order in both reports, so a note's edge is assigned by row index rather than by identity. And 12_search.report.json records no search at all - region 'chat', empty composer, the ordinary tail of the thread as its six visible ids - so the region reporter has no view onto the one thing that scene exists to show. Its video-row pixel count also does not reproduce from the box it names (3,104 of 64,542 measured, not 495 of 43,200), and it read MANIFEST's 'fourteen stale' as one old picture when DIFF shows six artifacts re-rendered since the baseline, one of them three minutes before the window opened.
